question:
A college library studies a collection of books using the number of pages in each book. On the set $B$ of all books in the library, a relation $R$ is defined by $xRy$ if and only if book $x$ and book $y$ have the same number of pages. For a small sample, books $P,Q,R,S,T$ contain $180,240,180,300,240$ pages respectively. The librarian wants to know whether this rule consistently groups books into classes and therefore examines the mathematical properties of the relation.

(a) From the given sample, find all books related to $P$.

(b) Show that the relation is reflexive.

(c) Show that the relation is symmetric.

(d) Verify transitivity and hence determine whether the relation is an equivalence relation.
explanation:
(a)
Book $P$ has $180$ pages. Among the given books, $R$ also has $180$ pages, while $Q$ and $T$ have $240$ pages and $S$ has $300$ pages. Since every book is also related to itself, the books related to $P$ are $P$ and $R$.

(b)
Every book has the same number of pages as itself. Therefore, for every book $x\in B$, $xRx$. Hence, $R$ is reflexive.

(c)
Suppose $xRy$. Then $x$ and $y$ have the same number of pages. Therefore, $y$ and $x$ also have the same number of pages, so $yRx$. Hence, $R$ is symmetric.

(d)
Suppose $xRy$ and $yRz$. Then $x$ and $y$ have the same number of pages, and $y$ and $z$ have the same number of pages. Therefore, $x$ and $z$ have the same number of pages, so $xRz$. Thus, $R$ is transitive. Since the relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, it is an equivalence relation.

options.A: Only book $R$ is related to $P$; the relation is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive, so it is not an equivalence relation.
options.B: Books $P,Q$ and $R$ are related to $P$; the relation is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive, so it is not an equivalence relation.
options.C: Books $P$ and $R$ are related to $P$; the relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so it is an equivalence relation.
options.D: Books $P$ and $T$ are related to $P$; the relation is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, so it is not an equivalence relation.
